compiled:
📰 General

Paramount Upholds Strategy, Retaining Cable Networks Post-WBD Merger •

Following the proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery, Paramount executives confirmed the company intends to maintain ownership of its existing cable networks. CEO David Ellison and COO Andy Gordon stated that no legacy cable networks are slated for sale as part of the combined entity. This decision contrasts with other media companies’ strategies to divest assets following similar consolidations. The move signals a commitment to continuing Paramount’s established cable programming portfolio.

🌍 World

Macron Announces France Will Share Nuclear-Armed Jets with Allies •

French President Emmanuel Macron announced a significant shift in French defense policy, stating the nation will bolster its nuclear arsenal. Under this new strategy, France will permit the temporary deployment of its nuclear-armed aircraft to allied countries for deterrence purposes. This marks the first time France has offered this capability, responding to concerns about Russia’s actions and bolstering NATO’s defenses. The move has been met with cautious reactions from allies, primarily focused on the logistical and strategic implications of the arrangement.

🦅 US

Austin Police Identify Suspect in West Sixth Street Mass Shooting; Three Dead •

Austin police have identified Ndiaga Diagne, 53, as the individual responsible for the shooting on West Sixth Street. The incident resulted in the deaths of three people, including Diagne himself, and left fourteen others with injuries. Authorities are still investigating the motive behind the attack. Details regarding Diagne’s background and prior history remain limited at this time. The investigation is ongoing with no further details released.

💰 Business

Netflix CEO Sarandos Details Strategic Shift Following Warner Bros. Deal Collapse •

Netflix CEO Ted Sarandos has discussed the company’s decision to abandon its pursuit of Warner Bros. Discovery. The streaming giant initially aimed to acquire the media conglomerate, but ultimately withdrew its offer after protracted negotiations. Sarandos attributed the withdrawal to a shift in Warner Bros.’ strategy and a desire to focus on its own content creation. This marks a significant change in the media landscape, with Paramount now holding the rights to a substantial portion of Warner Bros.’ library.

💻 Technology

Call of Duty Introduces Black Ops Royale: A New Warzone Battle-Royale Mode •

Activision and Treyarch have unveiled Black Ops Royale, a new battle-royale mode for Call of Duty. The mode draws significant inspiration from the Blackout mode featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. Black Ops Royale will feature a 100-player experience with a focus on classic Call of Duty gameplay mechanics. Players will compete across a variety of maps and utilize a selection of weapons and equipment. The new mode is slated for release on PlayStation early next month.

🎭 Entertainment

‘Hoppers’ Delivers Dark Humor and a Shocking Death in New Pixar Film •

Pixar’s latest film, ‘Hoppers,’ features a significant and unexpected death of a character approximately halfway through the narrative. The scene unfolds during a seemingly ordinary moment, creating a jarring and impactful shift in the storyline. A well-known actor voices the deceased character, adding to the surprise. Critics are praising the film’s darkly comedic tone and the effectiveness of this particular dramatic beat.

🏅 Sports

Chiefs Kingdom’s Jeremiyah Love Draft Hope Dashed by Todd McShay’s Projection •

NFL draft analyst Todd McShay recently projected that Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love will be the most popular draft target for Kansas City Chiefs fans. McShay’s assessment stems from Love’s perceived potential as a dynamic playmaker and his favorable draft stock. The projection represents a significant shift in Chiefs’ draft strategy, as Love was previously considered a potential first-round selection. This news has dampened enthusiasm among Chiefs fans regarding the 2026 NFL Draft.

🔬 Science

Massive Dinosaur Fossil Challenges Previous Size Estimates from the Cretaceous Period •

A remarkably well-preserved dinosaur fossil unearthed in Spain provides new evidence regarding the size of large theropods during the Late Cretaceous period. The fossil, discovered in 2014 at La Buitrera, represents a previously unknown species of theropod, tentatively named Buitreraptor. Researchers from the University of Minnesota analyzed the bones, revealing a creature significantly larger than previously estimated for dinosaurs of its age. The findings, published in Nature, suggest a more diverse range of sizes within theropod dinosaurs than previously understood.

🩺 Health

Common Health Conditions Significantly Raise Risk of Developing Dementia, Study Finds •

A new study has identified over 70 prevalent health conditions linked to an increased risk of developing dementia. Alzheimer’s disease, the most common form of dementia, currently affects approximately seven million Americans and is experiencing a nationwide rise in incidence. Researchers found a strong correlation between these conditions and the development of cognitive decline. The study highlights the importance of managing common ailments to potentially mitigate future dementia risk.
